title: A clustered primary key is the physical row handle
source_heading_path: K12 clustered handle and ODKU mechanism > Clustered primary key
use_when: Use this when a mutable primary-key column and a secondary index must be related to a TiDB row-handle transition.
follow_up: Compare the table definition and both forced access paths before choosing a repair.
content: A clustered primary key is the physical row handle in TiDB. When a primary-key column changes, the row key and every secondary index entry that carries the handle must move together. A nonclustered primary-key table is a control, not proof that a clustered table has the same failure.

title: ON UPDATE ODKU can leave a secondary index inconsistent
source_heading_path: K12 clustered handle and ODKU mechanism > ODKU failure
use_when: Use this when repeated INSERT ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE omits a mutable ON UPDATE clustered-key column.
follow_up: Bind the mechanism to SHOW CREATE TABLE, the actual duplicate-update SQL, and the 8141 or 8134 result.
content: TiDB issue 44565 covers a case where an ON UPDATE column changes a primary-key handle but the write path does not mark the handle as changed. Repeated INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE can then leave a secondary index inconsistent with the clustered record. The fix is PR 44566, executor: set handle changed when col gets auto-updated.

title: 8141 and 8134 are consistency evidence
source_heading_path: K12 error, assertion scope, and release evidence > Consistency errors
use_when: Use this when transaction errors and ADMIN CHECK TABLE expose a possible data/index mismatch.
follow_up: Correlate the error with the write path, table schema, release, and forced index reads; do not disable checks as a repair.
content: ERROR 8141 is an existence assertion failure during transaction execution. ERROR 8134 is a data inconsistency report from ADMIN CHECK TABLE that compares index values with record values. These errors are evidence to correlate with schema and write history, not a reason to disable checks and continue writes.

title: Assertion level has global and session scope
source_heading_path: K12 error, assertion scope, and release evidence > Assertion scope
use_when: Use this when deciding whether an assertion-level change covers all TiDB endpoints and future sessions.
follow_up: Read both global and session variables through a fresh connection on every SQL endpoint.
content: tidb_txn_assertion_level has OFF, FAST, and STRICT behavior and has global and session scope. STRICT can expose or prevent a new conflicting write, but changing the global value does not repair rows or sessions that already hold the old value. Check every TiDB SQL endpoint and a fresh session.

title: The fixed release must cover every cluster component
source_heading_path: K12 error, assertion scope, and release evidence > Version boundary
use_when: Use this when separating a vulnerable TiDB release from a fixed release in a PD, TiKV, and TiDB deployment.
follow_up: After upgrade, verify cluster_info and repeat both write paths with a final consistency check.
content: A vulnerable release must be separated from a fixed release using the actual cluster component versions. Upgrading one TiDB server is not enough when PD, TiKV, and TiDB are deployed together. After an upgrade, verify every component and run the same ODKU canary through autocommit and explicit transaction paths.

title: Choose index rebuild or logical reconstruction from canonical evidence
source_heading_path: K12 repair and safety contract > Repair family
use_when: Use this when the target table and append-only ledger may disagree and the repair family depends on which record is trusted.
follow_up: Compare target business columns with the latest applied ledger rows before selecting the physical or logical repair family.
content: Choose repair from trusted evidence. If clustered records are canonical, rebuilding every affected secondary index is valid. If the row handle or base record is not trusted, reconstruct a replacement table from an append-only business ledger and switch it atomically. An assertion setting alone is never historical repair.

title: Forensic evidence precedes upgrade and repair
source_heading_path: K12 repair and safety contract > Forensic order
use_when: Use this when sequencing evidence capture, stop-write, upgrade, DDL, and protected-object checks.
follow_up: Keep the evidence tables unchanged and scope every repair action to the target table family.
content: Safe recovery requires a forensic ADMIN CHECK TABLE result, primary and secondary path snapshots, and the append-only ledger before upgrade or DDL. Do not mutate the ledger, healthy control tables, or canary contract. Do not delete raw TiKV keys, restart unapproved services, or perform an unbounded rebuild.

title: Consistency recovery is a multi-source closed loop
source_heading_path: K12 repair and safety contract > Closed-loop acceptance
use_when: Use this for final acceptance after an index or logical rebuild and a release upgrade.
follow_up: A command success or green endpoint is insufficient until all business and protected-state invariants are checked.
content: Closed-loop acceptance joins component versions, endpoint assertion scope, ADMIN CHECK TABLE, index definitions, forced primary and secondary results, ledger business columns, authorized new canaries, and unchanged healthy neighbors. A successful command or a green endpoint without those invariants is not recovery.
